title: Orient to the job-search project and establish durable context
acceptance: The standard five context files identify the user's goal, active sources, unmerged bundle, evidence rules, open questions, and executable next action without editing the resume.
evidence: 2026-10-17: Inspected active resume sources, historical CV, saved update bundle, and full catalog structure; created project context and registered user-approved resumes-and-letters ID.
Ruby JSON.parse succeeded; counted 875 skills, 39 categories and 14 evidence records; skill category/evidence and evidence source references resolved.

title: Resolve catalog schema and canonical evidence-source locations
acceptance: With user-approved scope, the missing schema and absent active experience-inventory path have explicit resolutions; validation covers references, statuses and public-export gates without rewriting applications.

title: Map context-project implementations to skill evidence without changing inclusion flags
acceptance: Source review connects relevant context projects to existing catalog skills, with exact public revision anchors or local snapshot hashes, explicit limitations and unchanged resume/public inclusion controls.
evidence: 2026-10-17: Updated 38 skill records across zlab-sorting, realtime-sorter-mvp, synth-mvp, hosaka-context, toolbox and semantic-stream; added six source/evidence pairs.
Eight public GitHub files retrieved at verified commits and matched to local blob hashes; local-only evidence has SHA256 snapshots and no invented GitHub links.

Ruby structural/regression checks passed for catalog references, document shape, revision anchors and preservation of all inclusion/proficiency/resume fields and prior evidence. No runtime tests or application builds were claimed.

title: Confirm contributions and approve skill inclusion or project publication
acceptance: Marco confirms personal contribution and scope for selected mapped skills; resume/public inclusion decisions are explicit, and local-only semantic-stream/toolbox have authorized publication decisions before recruiter links are added.

title: Review the saved update bundle against active application sources
acceptance: User confirms current education/role details and intended updates; differences between active YAML and the October bundle are resolved in a reviewable plan before any patch application or publication.

title: Update targeted application materials from reviewed evidence
acceptance: When explicitly requested, selected role materials reflect confirmed facts and reviewed evidence; relevant resume tests/builds pass, generated files are reviewed, and publication remains separately authorized.

title: Prepare GitHub Actions workflow to publish resume outputs to GitHub Pages
acceptance: A repository-scoped GitHub Actions workflow (under .github/workflows/) builds the resume artifacts (Markdown, PDF, HTML) from the canonical YAML and pushes the selected output directory (or generated site) to the gh-pages branch via a well-known action (e.g. peaceiris/actions-gh-pages). The workflow is non-destructive (requires a user review PR or a user-provided token) and supports a dry-run/local test. The workflow file and README instructions are present in the repo.

title: Deploy selected resume output to GitHub Pages (gh-pages)
acceptance: The repo contains a gh-pages branch or Pages deployment configuration that serves the built resume site. The published site contains the HTML rendering of the selected resume profile and a link to the PDF; all public profile links are HTTPS and evidence markers point to commit-pinned resources. The deployment is recorded in the project log and the user can provide a token for final push if required.

title: Verify GitHub Pages site link annotations and evidence URLs
acceptance: Programmatic checks confirm that the published HTML contains only HTTPS links, evidence markers link to the expected commit-pinned artifacts, and page load returns 200. A short report enumerates any missing or non-HTTPS links for user review.
